ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Quantifying burden

A 51-year-old has frequent palpitations and PVCs on a brief office tracing. The cardiologist wants to determine what proportion of all beats are ventricular ectopic beats and whether symptoms coincide with them. Which test is most directly suited to that goal?

  1. Resting pulse oximetry
  2. Carotid ultrasonography
  3. Ambulatory ECG monitoring
  4. A single serum troponin level
  5. Chest radiography
Answer and explanation

Ambulatory ECG monitoring

Ambulatory recording quantifies frequency over time and can correlate symptoms.

Option explanations

Ambulatory ECG monitoring: Ambulatory recording quantifies frequency over time and can correlate symptoms.

A single serum troponin level: Troponin assesses myocardial injury rather than ectopic burden.

Chest radiography: A radiograph cannot count ectopic beats.

Resting pulse oximetry: Oxygen saturation does not establish the rhythm.

Carotid ultrasonography: Carotid imaging does not quantify ventricular ectopy.
